name: Tretinoin
summary: The gold-standard retinoid: builds collagen, smooths fine wrinkles, clears acne, reverses photoaging.

name: Retinol
summary: OTC vitamin-A derivative; converts to retinoic acid in skin.
note: Weaker than tretinoin but no prescription needed.

name: Adapalene
summary: OTC retinoid for acne and texture — the strongest retinoid you can buy without a script.

name: Tazarotene
summary: Potent topical retinoid for acne and photoaging.

name: Isotretinoin
summary: Systemic retinoid for severe, treatment-resistant acne.

name: Botulinum toxin A
summary: Relaxes facial muscles to erase dynamic wrinkles.

name: Azelaic acid
summary: Triple threat: acne, redness, and dark spots in one ingredient.

name: Niacinamide
summary: Barrier support, oil control, and pigment evening.

name: Vitamin C (topical)
summary: Antioxidant that brightens, fades spots, and supports collagen pathways.

name: Tranexamic acid
summary: Melasma and stubborn hyperpigmentation fighter, topical or oral (oral = Rx).

name: Hydroquinone
summary: The strongest proven pigment suppressor for dark spots.

name: Alpha-arbutin
summary: Gentler tyrosinase inhibitor for dark spots.

name: Kojic acid
summary: Fungal-derived tyrosinase inhibitor used in brightening products.

name: Cysteamine
summary: Topical depigmenting agent with solid melasma studies.

name: Salicylic acid
summary: Oil-soluble BHA that gets inside pores and unclogs them.

name: Glycolic acid
summary: AHA exfoliant for glow, texture, and surface renewal.

name: Lactic acid
summary: Gentler AHA that exfoliates and hydrates at once.

name: Ceramides
summary: Rebuild the skin barrier and lock in moisture.

name: Urea
summary: Humectant + keratolytic that fixes rough, dry, flaky skin.

name: Hyaluronic acid
summary: Holds ~1000x its weight in water. Hydration and temporary plumping; injectable forms are fillers.

name: GHK-Cu
summary: Copper peptide tied to collagen remodeling, wound repair, and follicle biology. Topical evidence only.
note: FDA flagged injectable versions as a significant safety risk.

name: Matrixyl
summary: Cosmetic signaling peptide marketed for collagen and fine lines.

name: Argireline
summary: The "topical Botox" claim. Evidence is thin.

name: SNAP-8
summary: Expression-line cosmetic peptide, same family as Argireline.

name: Carnosine
summary: Antioxidant + antiglycation dipeptide studied for skin aging.

name: Spironolactone
summary: Antiandrogen used for hormonal acne in the right patients. Also a diuretic.

name: Clascoterone
summary: Topical antiandrogen approved for acne; being studied for hair loss.

name: PDRN / Polynucleotides
summary: Salmon-DNA "skin boosters" marketed for regeneration and repair. Formulation-dependent.

name: Omega-3 (EPA/DHA)
summary: Anti-inflammatory fats relevant to skin, recovery, and general health.

name: Zinc
summary: May calm inflammatory acne; fixes deficiency-related hair shedding.
note: Strong only when you were actually deficient.
